PullRequest.Title: fix: check command links in untrusted workspace Markdown files
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Scenarios.Scenario: Click an allowed command link originating from an editor, webview/Markdown preview, or notebook while the workspace is untrusted
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user click calls IOpenerService.open, validators run before the CommandOpener, and the changed validator awaits requestWorkspaceTrust. The command cannot execute until the user accepts or cancels; this intentional modal trust decision is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await an in-process modal workspace-trust dialog driven by the request service event
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active dialog for any number of concurrent command-link opens; one new request per later click after cancellation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The opener validator immediately accepted non-HTTP(S) command URIs, so no workspace-trust dialog was on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that command open until the user responds, as required by the security decision

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with command-link click attempts, not with the number of links rendered. Only command URIs whose command is enabled by allowCommands and whose caller sets fromWorkspace reach the new request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: WorkspaceTrustRequestService stores one active promise and returns it to subsequent callers, so concurrent clicks coalesce into one modal request rather than creating a prompt burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A trusted workspace takes the synchronous trust-state fast path. While a request is active it is coalesced. Acceptance changes the authoritative trust state; cancellation clears the request promise, so a later explicit click can ask again without retaining unbounded state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added modal critical path and coalescing because both the changed await and WorkspaceTrustRequestService's shared promise were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Human click frequency and dialog response time vary, but rendered document size does not multiply this work and active requests are coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The latency is the explicit trust gate required by the behavior change, is user-triggered, and is coalesced under concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open ordinary HTTP(S), file, and other non-command string resources through IOpenerService
Scenarios.CriticalPath: IOpenerService already parses string targets once. The changed validator now parses the string a second time before its scheme checks, then existing validators/openers and any target-specific external opening continue as before.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional URI parse and object allocation per string-valued open, linear in the URI string length. Typical opens are user actions and no changed loop, render path, startup path, or realistic bulk caller was established.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed queue, limiter, or fan-out; each independent open performs its own bounded parse exactly once in this validator.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved or defeated. URI-valued callers avoid parsing in the changed validator; string targets receive no parse cache, as before in the opener service.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that duplicate parsing is introduced, but low confidence that its tiny bounded CPU/allocation cost can create user-visible degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: There may be programmatic callers with higher rates, but the inspected changed paths and primary link callers are user-triggered; no realistic hot/scaling path was evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is bounded in-memory work with no proven hot or collection-scaled trigger and does not meet the actionable regression threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and restored-phase registration of the opener validator
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The validator contribution is created at LifecyclePhase.Restored. The added constructor dependency resolves IWorkspaceTrustRequestService, but WorkspaceTrustRequestHandler already depends on and instantiates that delayed singleton during WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one contribution and one service instance per workbench window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous dependency injection only; no changed parallel work or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The DI singleton is reused; the diff does not create another service instance or cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added dependency does not newly instantiate the service on startup because an earlier BlockRestore contribution already requires it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: registration phases and singleton ownership were inspected directly.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced command-link opening, ordinary URI opening, trust-request coalescing, modal ownership, and startup instantiation. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
